items.text: Cheng's House, Ancient Zhu County
The cold sky presses down on black tiles. Black tiles press down on white walls.
At the foot of these walls is a courtyard. Though swept clean that morning, a light dusting of snow has already begun to reclaim it.
Chéng Héguāng carries firewood into the house and lights the stove.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Copying documents at the Yamen still earns me around 30 wen a day.
He takes the ledger and inkstone down from a nearby shelf, dips his brush in ink, and carefully records the day's income and expenses.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: One bass sold for seven wen.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Expenses: leaf celery, four wen. One jin of salt, five wen. Medicinal herbs, ten wen.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Hm?
Someone steps lightly behind him and drapes a coat over his shoulders.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Back already? *cough* My, every winter feels colder than the last.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: You should be in bed. I only went to see Doctor Wú for some Baibu; he said you should be resting.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Alright, alright. But why did you go to him again? Don't you usually go to Jishitang?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I wanted a new prescription. I heard he'd just made a new batch of Dazao pills.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Did you get some?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: *sigh* I told you not to go there! In fact, I said we should've cut ties with him long ago.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Started up with his usual nonsense, did he? Refusing to let you inside, using some "illness" as an excuse? *cough, cough*
Chéng pauses for a moment and closes the ledger.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It's no matter. I have the medicine. I'll start brewing it now.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: What did he say?
At the doorway, the branches of a Mei tree shake off a few clumps of snow.
Thankfully for him, a sudden knock at the door interrupts the awkward silence.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Expecting someone?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: We haven't had a visitor since your uncle returned to the countryside.
Chéng puts the ledger back on the shelf.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I'll take a look.
Chéng trudges back through the snow to the courtyard gate and raises the latch.
A familiar military officer stands outside.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Commander Lì?

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Hmm. Héguāng, I hope I'm not intruding.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Not at all. I just returned from the clinic and was preparing to brew some medicine.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: How is your mother these days?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Consumption is not easy to treat.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Are you here on official Yamen business?
Lì Huìfēng offers a faint, amiable smile.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: The Yamen's affairs have nothing to do with me.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: I'm here to offer you an opportunity.
Chéng returns indoors, clutching a yellowed sheet of paper.
The lid of the pot on the stove has already been lifted, the cooked rice porridge inside sending steady curls of steam into the air.
Out of habit, he takes the ladle from his mother's hand.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Let me take care of this.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Who was it at the door, then?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It was Commander Lì.
Chéng brings the porridge to the wooden table and casually passes the paper to his mother.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Tomorrow, I'll ask if Auntie can come lend her hand for a while.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It will be a long journey.
A few sparrows flit past the window, chirping as they flutter out of the courtyard.
Street, Riverside Village
This small village, governed by another county of Huanzhou Prefecture and nestled between mountains and rivers, has simply come to be called the Riverside Village.
This Riverside Village looks much like Zhu County. At its entrance, Chéng Héguāng sees the familiar rise and fall of black tiles once again.
Only, today's early afternoon is not quite as peaceful as usual.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: My brother's been mauled by a tiger! He's damn near on his deathbed! And you dogs have the gall to stand here, pushing us around?!
To the left of the village entrance stands an exceptionally grand courtyard, with a memorial Paifang outside bearing the words "Loyalty, Filial Piety, Integrity, and Righteousness."
A group of villagers have gathered beneath the Paifang, their faces flushed as they shout at the household guards blocking their way.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Likely the residence of a local gentry.
Chéng approaches without a word, slipping in among several bystanders.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: Doctor Xiù was paid for with the family's hard-earned silver! She's inside treating Master Hú. How dare you try to barge in!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Doctor Xiù is the village physician, not the Hú family's private attendant!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: What could be more urgent than a life-or-death situation?! What right do you have to stop us? What are you hiding in there?

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Tell Doctor Xiù there's a patient out here on the verge of death! I know she'll come out to save him!

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: You'll just have to find another doctor. If you set off now for the county, you can make it there before nightfall.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: We already hauled him all the way down the mountain to Doctor Xiù's clinic, only to be told she was here!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Just look at him! Does he look as though he'll survive a trip to the county?!
The injured villager is slumped over his companion's back, his hastily bandaged left arm soaked with blood.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: That's none of our concern. We had no hand in his injuries.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: If you continue causing a scene outside Master Hú's house, we'll call the bailiff over to have you arrested!
The lead villager explodes in fury.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Go on, call him! You're all in cahoots with one another anyway!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Hú Hǎiyuè is so afraid of dying. He summons a doctor every time he nicks his skin.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: Watch your mouth, you slanderer!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Our man's been mauled half to death, and you won't even let him through the door!

items.speaker: Calm Villager
items.text: They waited until land prices were low and took two acres of my land in exchange for just one tael of silver.

items.speaker: Disheartened Villager
items.text: Last year, I had a funeral to arrange and was desperate for money. The Hú family loaned it to me but charged five percent interest.
The lead villager snatches a bow from his companion's hands and aims it at the household guards. A wave of shock ripples through them.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: The Hú family's out to ruin us all! First they snatch up our fields, then they hound us with debt! They're driving us to death!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Fellow villagers, tell me, does this sound fair to you?!

items.speaker: Villagers
items.text: No!
The rest of the villagers shout, their hoes and clubs raised high.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: We're done waiting! We're not taking it anymore!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: One way or another, I am going through that door!

items.speaker: Villagers
items.text: We'll not be pushed around! Burn down the gate! We'll force our way in!
The household guards draw their swords, raising their shields into a solid wall.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: Go ahead and try! This is nothing short of rebellion.
Before the words even finish leaving the guard's mouth, an arrow flies toward his forehead.
But before it can strike, it is cleaved in two by a flash of steel.
Chéng sheaths his blade, stepping between the guards and the villagers.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: This man is dying! What harm is there in letting him inside?

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: Who are you?!

items.speaker: Calm Villager
items.text: He's not one of us.
The crowd exchanges glances like a theater troupe interrupted mid-performance, unsure of what to do next.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: You—
The gate is suddenly thrown open.
What is going on out there?!
